high.title: US Strikes Iran Again: Root Cause Revealed
high.summary: The US launched retaliatory strikes against Iran on June 25 after Iran attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, violating an existing ceasefire agreement. The US targeted Iranian missile storage facilities, drone sites, and coastal radar installations. This escalation threatens global oil supply routes through the Strait of Hormuz, which could drive up global energy prices and impact Indonesia's trade and commodity markets.

high.title: Government Collects Rp 52.85 Trillion from Crypto and Fintech Taxes – Breakdown Revealed
high.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxation (DJP) has collected Rp 52.85 trillion in digital economy tax revenue through May 31, 2026, with the bulk coming from VAT on electronic commerce (Rp 40.55 trillion), followed by fintech/P2P lending taxes (Rp 4.98 trillion), government procurement taxes (Rp 5.26 trillion), and crypto asset taxes (Rp 2.06 trillion). The consistent year-on-year growth in digital tax collection signals expanding regulatory reach over the digital economy sector. This is significant for investors in fintech, crypto, and e-commerce businesses operating in Indonesia as compliance and tax burdens continue to rise.

high.title: Chicken Prices Collapse to Rp 13,000/kg at Farm Level, Far Below Production Cost
high.summary: Farmgate chicken prices have plummeted to Rp 13,000/kg in West Java, well below the production cost of Rp 22,000–23,000/kg, creating a severe financial crisis for independent poultry farmers since April 2026. The collapse is compounded by the school holiday season halting the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, reducing demand significantly. Farmers are urging the government to reinstate a social assistance program that previously distributed chicken and eggs to 1.5 million beneficiaries, which would help absorb excess supply.

high.title: US Strikes Iran Again: Root Cause Revealed
high.summary: The US launched military strikes against Iranian missile storage sites, drones, and coastal radar installations after Iran attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, which the US deemed a violation of the existing ceasefire agreement. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global oil and trade chokepoint, and escalating tensions could significantly impact global commodity prices, shipping costs, and energy markets. Indonesian investors should monitor potential ripple effects on global oil prices and supply chain disruptions.

high.title: Customs Intercepts Thai National Carrying USD 350,000 (IDR 6.3 Billion) at Soekarno-Hatta Airport
high.summary: Indonesian Customs at Soekarno-Hatta Airport seized USD 350,000 in cash (equivalent to IDR 6.3 billion) from a Thai national who was carrying the foreign currency without proper authorization, as part of efforts to maintain monetary stability and financial sovereignty. The enforcement highlights Indonesia's strict cross-border cash monitoring regulations, which require declaration of large foreign currency amounts. This is relevant to businesses and investors engaged in cross-border financial transactions and foreign exchange flows.

high.title: Prabowo Plans to Close 750 State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) That Are Unprofitable and Only Paying Overhead
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto announced plans to shut down more than 750 state-owned enterprises (SOEs) that fail to generate profits while continuing to burden the state budget with large executive salaries and overhead costs. This major restructuring of Indonesia's SOE sector signals a significant shift in state enterprise policy and could have wide-ranging implications for employment, government finances, and related industries. Investors in SOE-linked stocks and sectors should monitor which specific entities are targeted for closure.

high.title: Prabowo's Advisor Reveals Unavoidable Mass Layoffs: 2,500 Workers at PT Pakerin to Be Dismissed
high.summary: Presidential Special Advisor for Labor Affairs Said Iqbal confirmed that PT Pakerin in Mojokerto, East Java, will inevitably proceed with mass layoffs affecting 2,500 workers. Around Rp 159 billion in funds held by PT Pakerin at Bank Prima will be liquidated through the Deposit Insurance Corporation (LPS) to cover severance payments. This case highlights ongoing labor market stress in Indonesian manufacturing and raises questions about the health of the banking sector's exposure to struggling industrial firms.

high.title: New Outsourcing Regulation Due in July: Only 4 Job Types Permitted for Contract Workers
high.summary: A revised Ministerial Regulation (Permenaker No. 7/2026) on outsourcing is set to be issued by mid-July 2026, effectively banning the practice except for four supporting job categories: catering staff, security, drivers, and cleaning services. Companies will be given a 6-month transition period to comply, which could significantly increase labor costs and restructuring needs across multiple industries. This regulation is a major labor policy shift that will impact businesses heavily reliant on outsourced or contract workers.

high.title: Prabowo Plans to Close 750 State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) That Are Unprofitable and Only Paying Overhead
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto announced plans to shut down over 750 state-owned enterprises (SOEs) that are generating no profit while continuing to burden state finances with large executive salaries and overhead costs. This sweeping SOE restructuring signals a major shift in Indonesia's state enterprise policy that could significantly impact employment, government finances, and related listed subsidiaries. Investors in SOE-linked stocks and bonds should monitor developments closely as consolidation may create both risks and opportunities.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Rp 8,000/gram in One Week; Buyback Price Drops Rp 20,000/gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices moved volatilely during the June 22–27, 2026 trading week, closing down Rp 8,000 per gram at Rp 2,660,000/gram. The sharpest single-day drop occurred on Wednesday June 24 with a Rp 18,000/gram decline, while the buyback price also fell significantly by Rp 20,000/gram. This is relevant for retail investors holding gold as a safe-haven asset and for tracking broader commodity sentiment in Indonesia.

medium.title: Chicken Prices at Market Also Plunge to Rp 35,000/kg — Here's the Root Cause
medium.summary: Farm-gate chicken prices have collapsed to as low as Rp 13,000/kg in West Java since April 2026, far below the cost of production at Rp 22,000–23,000/kg, causing severe losses for independent poultry farmers. The crisis is compounded by the school holiday season halting the government's Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program, reducing demand absorption. Farmers are urging the government to reinstate poultry as part of social assistance programs to stabilize prices and protect livelihoods in the sector.

medium.title: Prabowo Questions Whether State-Owned Enterprises Even Have Profits After Proposal to Fund Research from SOE Earnings
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto responded to a proposal to allocate a portion of State-Owned Enterprise (BUMN) profits toward research and innovation funding, calling the idea good but openly questioning whether SOEs are actually profitable. His remarks highlight ongoing concerns about the financial performance and accountability of Indonesia's BUMN sector. This signals a potential policy review of SOE profitability expectations and could influence investor sentiment toward BUMN-linked stocks.

medium.title: 8% App Commission Cut for Ride-Hailing (Ojol) May Extend to Online Taxis, Says Transport Minister
medium.summary: Indonesia's Minister of Transportation Dudy Purwagandhi confirmed that the new regulation capping app platform commissions at 8% currently applies only to two-wheeled ride-hailing services (ojol), not online taxis. The government is studying whether the policy could be extended to four-wheeled online taxi services in the future. This regulation is material for investors in gig economy platforms such as Gojek and Grab, as it directly impacts their revenue model and commission structures.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Rp 8,000/gram Over the Week, Buyback Price Drops Rp 20,000/gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices ended the week of June 22–27, 2026 down Rp 8,000/gram, closing at Rp 2,660,000/gram after a volatile week that included an Rp 18,000/gram single-day drop on Wednesday. The buyback price also fell sharply by Rp 20,000/gram, indicating weaker demand or global gold price pressure. Indonesian retail investors holding physical gold should note the downward trend, which may reflect broader global commodity market movements.

medium.title: Revealed: Japanese Automotive Giants That Planned to Leave Indonesia But Were Prevented
medium.summary: PT JAI in Pasuruan and PT SAI in Mojokerto, both part of the Yazaki Group, have scaled back plans to relocate 50% of their production lines to Vietnam following dialogue between management and labor unions, with only 3-5 production lines now being moved. This is a positive development for Indonesian industrial employment and the automotive supply chain, signaling that labor-management negotiations can help retain foreign investment. The outcome is significant for investors tracking Indonesia's competitiveness as a manufacturing hub amid ongoing relocation pressures to Southeast Asian rivals.

medium.title: Ministry of Transportation Speaks Out on the Fate of High-Speed Rail Extension to Surabaya
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Transportation has indicated that plans to extend the Whoosh high-speed rail from Bandung to Surabaya remain uncertain, as the government is prioritizing the financial restructuring of the existing Jakarta-Bandung high-speed rail project before committing to further expansion. The statement aligns with directives from Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure Agus Harimurti Yudhoyono, who chairs the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Rail Committee. This is relevant for infrastructure-related stocks and investors tracking Indonesia's large-scale rail and connectivity projects.

medium.title: Tax Authority Appoints 7 New Digital Tax Collectors Including Strava
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) has designated seven new entities as VAT collectors for digital economy transactions (PMSE), including Strava Inc, Envato, Kling AI, and the Law School Admission Council, among others. This move reflects the government's continued effort to broaden the digital tax base and capture revenue from foreign digital service providers operating in Indonesia. Businesses and consumers using these platforms in Indonesia will now be subject to VAT on their transactions.

medium.title: Prabowo's Advisor Calls for Zero Tax on BPJS Employment Retirement Fund (JHT) Withdrawals
medium.summary: Presidential Advisor Said Iqbal argued that taxing JHT (old-age security) withdrawals from BPJS Ketenagakerjaan constitutes double taxation, since workers' wages are already subject to income tax (PPh 21) before contributions are made. He is proposing a 0% tax rate on JHT disbursements as a pro-worker policy measure. If adopted, this change could meaningfully increase the net retirement benefits received by millions of Indonesian workers and affect government income tax revenues.

medium.title: Broiler Chicken Farmers Cry Out as Farm-Gate Prices Plunge to IDR 13,000/kg
medium.summary: Live broiler chicken prices at the farm gate have collapsed to as low as IDR 13,000–14,000/kg in West Java, down sharply from IDR 18,000/kg since April 2026, according to the Indonesian Independent Poultry Farmers Association (Permindo). The steep price decline is causing significant financial distress for small-scale poultry farmers and could impact companies across the poultry supply chain. This development may affect listed poultry and feed companies such as CPIN, JPFA, and MAIN.

medium.title: Yazaki Group's Two Japanese Automotive Component Plants in Indonesia Retain Most Production, Avoid Mass Relocation to Vietnam
medium.summary: PT JAI (Pasuruan) and PT SAI (Mojokerto), both part of Japan's Yazaki Group, have scaled back plans to relocate 50% of their production lines to Vietnam after successful negotiations between management and labor unions, with only 3–5 production lines now being moved. This outcome is seen as a positive development for Indonesia's automotive manufacturing sector and labor market stability. The episode highlights ongoing concerns about Indonesia's competitiveness in retaining foreign industrial investment amid regional competition.

medium.title: Customs Authorities Intercept Thai National Carrying USD 350,000 (IDR 6.3 Billion) in Cash at Soekarno-Hatta Airport
medium.summary: Soekarno-Hatta Customs intercepted a Thai national carrying USD 350,000 in cash (3,500 x USD 100 bills) without proper authorization at Terminal 2F International Arrivals, as part of efforts to maintain monetary stability and enforce cross-border cash regulations. The case is under further customs investigation to assess corporate financial compliance. This action underscores Indonesia's tightening enforcement of foreign currency controls, which is relevant to businesses and individuals involved in cross-border financial transactions.

medium.title: Ministry of Transportation Speaks on Fate of High-Speed Rail Extension to Surabaya
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Transportation confirmed that any extension of the Whoosh high-speed rail beyond Bandung to Surabaya remains on hold, with the government prioritizing the financial restructuring of the existing Jakarta-Bandung project first. The statement aligns with directions from Coordinating Minister AHY, who chairs the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Rail Committee. This signals continued uncertainty for infrastructure investors and contractors eyeing the potential Surabaya extension project.

medium.title: DJP Appoints 7 New Digital Tax Collectors, Including Strava
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) has appointed seven new entities as VAT collectors for Electronic System Trade (PMSE) as of May 2026. The newly appointed collectors include Strava Inc, Envato Pty Ltd, Envato Elements Pty Ltd, The Nielsen Norman Group Inc, Kling AI Pte Ltd, Law School Admission Council Inc, and PLAUD LLC, covering sectors such as fitness, digital content, education, and AI. This move reflects Indonesia's continued efforts to broaden its digital economy tax base and ensure compliance from foreign digital service providers operating in the country.
